hibs.label: Daniel
hibs.reconciliation_note: extends the existing Daniel HIB (id 47, tracked from Dan 1/8) with its Dan 2 appearances -- same identity, not a correction of prior content.

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: the same named individual already tracked in Dan 1/8 -- continuity of a real person, not a fresh judgement call.
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: already a live HIB (id 47); this call only adds verses, never reintroduces a previously-excluded referent.
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: present as narrative actor vv13-26,46-49, and as the continuous speaker of his own discourse vv27-45 (the phase-1 sweep counts a speaker present throughout their own quoted speech, per Step 1's "speaks" criterion) -- verified against the narration/quotation structure verse by verse.

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: the same named individual already tracked in Dan 1/8.

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: named individual, "the captain of the king's guard" (v14) -- a real court office-holder, not a personification.
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: not previously recorded or excluded anywhere in the live Dan HIB register (checked against all 14 existing rows before this call).
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: v14 names him directly ("Arioch, the captain of the king's guard"); v15/24/25 each show him acting (making the matter known, being addressed by Daniel, bringing Daniel before the king).

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: the summoned professional class (magicians/enchanters/sorcerers/Chaldeans/astrologers, v2,10,27) -- real human courtiers, not a personified institution.
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: not previously recorded or excluded in the live Dan HIB register.
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: v2 lists the four professional titles summoned; v12-13 names them collectively "the wise men of Babylon" under threat of death; v48 confirms Daniel is later made "chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon" -- the same referent throughout. Modelled as ONE collective HIB (collective-stays-collective), consistent with the Dan 8 precedent ("the four kingdoms", id 27).

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: the unnamed party carrying out the death decree ("they sought Daniel and his companions, to kill them") -- human agents, not a personification.
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: not previously recorded or excluded in the live Dan HIB register.
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: lexical confirms a plain 3mp verb (H1156 AVqp3mp "they sought") with no named antecedent in v13 itself -- a genuine referential HIB per the referential-named-not-skipped rule, not asserted as Arioch's own identity since v13 itself does not name him (Arioch is named only in v14).

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: represents the human rulers/peoples of the kingdom that will arise after Nebuchadnezzar's, per the vision -- consistent with the Dan 8 precedent ("the four kingdoms", id 27) treating a prophetic kingdom as a trackable HIB.
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: not previously recorded or excluded in the live Dan HIB register.
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: v39a: "another kingdom inferior to you shall arise after you."

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: same grounds as "the second kingdom" -- represents a future kingdom's human rulers/peoples.
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: not previously recorded or excluded in the live Dan HIB register.
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: v39b: "yet a third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over all the earth."

quality_checks.is-genuinely-human: same grounds as the second/third kingdoms -- represents the fourth (and later divided) kingdom's human rulers/peoples, including v43's "they will mix with one another in marriage" (3mp verbs, lexically confirmed).
quality_checks.not-already-excluded: not previously recorded or excluded in the live Dan HIB register.
quality_checks.verse-actually-supports-it: v40 introduces it ("a fourth kingdom, strong as iron"); v41-43 elaborate its divided nature; v44's "in the days of those kings" ties temporally to this same kingdom's era.
